RFC8956-3.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: TestIPv6FlowPrefixPatternAndPadding moved verbatim to core internal/core/bgp/nlri/flowspec/rfc8956_prefix_test.go, with only the family identifier renamed (test-local AFI 2/SAFI 133). RFC 8956 Section 3.1: "Padding bits MUST be 0 on encoding and MUST be ignored on decoding." Encode clause: received patterns padded with 0xff must re-encode through both Bytes() and WriteTo to the canonical zero-padded bytes (0xff becomes 0xfe for 72/65, 0xff becomes 0xc0 for 17/7), and a configured 2001:db8:ffff::/33 must encode its last pattern octet as exactly 0x80.

RFC8956-3.1-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: same unit as RFC8956-3.1-1, moved verbatim to core. The quote carries both clauses. Encoding is proven by the canonical-bytes assertions. Decoding: inputs with 0xff padding must parse without error, and comp.Prefix() must equal the pattern-only prefix (::7f00:0:0:0/72, 103:8000::/17) with the exact offset. A decoder that read padding into the match, or rejected nonzero padding, fails require.NoError or the Prefix assertion.

RFC8956-3.1-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: both units changed only by package qualification. The plugin unit now calls core flowspec.ParseFlowSpec and flowspec.KwDestinationIPv6; the firewall unit names the IPv6 FlowSpec family as a family.Family literal. RFC 8956 Section 3.1: "If length = 0 and offset = 0, this component matches every address; otherwise, length MUST be in the range offset < length < 129 or the component is malformed." First clause: flowspec-firewall TestRFC8956ZeroLengthZeroOffsetMatchesEveryAddress parses 03 01 00 00 and 03 02 00 00 and requires the firewall matches to be exactly MatchDestinationAddress{::/0} and MatchSourceAddress{::/0}. Its containment loop checks the constant and adds nothing, so the require.Equal is the proof. Second clause: TestIPv6FlowPrefixRejectsMalformedBounds requires parse errors for 0/1, 64/64, 63/64, 129/0 and a truncated pattern, and config refusal for /64/64, /64/65 and /0/1. It also requires 80/64 to encode and compare equal to its received form.

RFC8956-3.6-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: the unit moved to core rfc8956_fragment_test.go. It changed only by the family identifiers and the now-exported NewFlowFragmentMatchComponent. RFC 8956 Section 3.6: "The Type 12 component bitmask MUST be encoded as a single octet bitmask (bitmask_op len=00)." A value of ^uint64(0) through the IPv6 FlowSpec and IPv6 VPN producers must encode exactly {12, 0x81, 0x0e} (len=00, one octet) via WriteTo and Bytes(), so core writeToAFI applies fragmentMask before choosing the width. The negative requires ParseFlowSpec/ParseFlowSpecVPN to refuse a 0x91 (len=01) two-octet operand.

RFC8956-3.6-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: the unit moved verbatim to core, with only the family identifiers renamed. RFC 8956 Section 3.6: "0: MUST be set to 0 on NLRI encoding". One shared component carrying DF|IsF, FF and LF must encode IPv6 and IPv6-VPN as 2, 4, 8 (DF, reserved in Figure 1, cleared), while IPv4 and IPv4-VPN keep 3. Core fragmentMask(AFIIPv6)=0x0e is what clears it. The high reserved bits are covered by the 3.6-1 unit.

RFC8956-3.6-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: the unit moved verbatim to core, with only the family identifiers renamed. The quote carries both clauses. Decoding: operands 0xf3, 0xf5, 0xf9, 0xf1, each carrying every reserved bit, must parse without error for IPv6 and IPv6-VPN, and Matches() must equal exactly IsF, FF, LF, 0. Encoding: the re-encoded NLRI must equal the input with reserved bits zeroed (2, 4, 8, 0).

RFC8956-5-1.note: Independent semantic rejudgment: RFC8956 Section 5: "A destination prefix component with offset=0 is embedded in the Flow Specification." Section 5 retains RFC8955 validation but replaces item a with this offset-zero amendment. Current TestFlowSpecVPNValidationSeparatesAFIAndRD uses a legal /64 offset32 four-byte pattern, the same RD/default authorizing route, and unchanged wire input. It requires retained receipt but false generation-7 eligibility, zero candidates and no additional selected event; the zero-offset rule succeeds. Removing only the Offset()==0 gate now fails that consumer oracle and clean controls pass. The pattern shape is legal under Section 3.1 length-minus-offset; rejection is authorization, not malformed encoding. Enforcement is for this amendment, not blanket inherited-rule or dataplane compliance. These are inspected scratch semantic executions, not canonical discrimination records. Current native record renewal/stamping remains parent-owned; no pending FRR carrier run, SRPM behavior, dataplane behavior, or full-RFC acceptance is inferred.
